---
name: unverified-counterexample-in-docstring
description: "Reaching for a prose counterexample to show a hypothesis is necessary is the tell that the iff you want is one mathlib lemma away"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When you want to show a binder is **necessary** rather than merely consumed, the
binder-deletion control only proves the name is used — knowing it is weak is what
pushes you toward prose, and prose is where unverified claims survive.

Measured on my own file (AJC, `Picard/GaloisDescent/GaloisSelfTensor.lean`, run 0083
r6, fixed at `7b135daed5`) before any reviewer saw it. I proved a Galois splitting
`L ⊗[K] L ≃ₐ[L] (Gal(L/K) → L)` under `[IsGalois K L]`, proved the dimension
converse (bijectivity ⟹ `#Aut = [L:K]`), and then wrote in the docstring that at
`ℚ(2^(1/3))/ℚ` we have `#Aut = 1 < 3 = [L:K]`, hence the conclusion fails there.
Every word true; **none of it checked**. The Lean content stopped at the dimension
count, and the step to "necessary" ran through an arithmetic fact about a specific
extension that existed only in prose — a sorry census, axiom check and vacuity sweep
all pass that.

The fix was shorter than the paragraph: `IsGalois.of_card_aut_eq_finrank` (Stacks
09I1 "if" part) is the *converse* of the lemma I had already used forward. Pairing
them gives **bijective ↔ IsGalois** for an arbitrary finite extension — no
counterexample needed, no separability binder, and it says more than the
counterexample would have.

**Why:** an unverified counterexample is the same defect as an unverified theorem,
sited where nobody re-checks. It also *understates*: an iff forecloses every route,
where a counterexample only blocks one.

**How to apply:** when you catch yourself writing "and at ⟨specific object⟩ the
conclusion fails", stop — ask whether the lemma you just proved has a named converse
in mathlib. Numerical criteria usually do, stated as iffs or as matched pairs
(`card_aut_eq_finrank` / `of_card_aut_eq_finrank`). Grep the same file the forward
lemma came from.

Related: [[check-the-statement-not-the-name]],
[[probe-the-adds-no-strength-claim]], [[a-control-that-cannot-fail-differently]],
[[measure-the-converse-before-strictly-weaker]].

---
name: private-index-protects-others-not-you
description: "A correctly-executed fresh private index still leaves your own file staged for deletion in the SHARED index; the two checks guard opposite directions"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Doing the fresh-private-index procedure perfectly does **not** stop your file being
staged for deletion in the shared index. Measured at AJC run 0083 r6 session end: I
committed `Picard/GaloisDescent/GaloisSelfTensor.lean` with a fresh index
(`rm -f`, `read-tree HEAD`, explicit `add`, verified stat, commit) and ran
`diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` after each of three commits — all clean, only my paths.
The shared index nonetheless listed that same file as a staged `D`, alongside four
other lanes' brand-new proof files (1702 deletion lines total). All seven present at
HEAD and on disk, so nothing was lost — but the next lane committing from the shared
index would have destroyed them.

The asymmetry is the point, and it is easy to misread as "the procedure failed":

* **fresh index + post-commit `diff HEAD~1 HEAD`** stops *you* clobbering *others*;
* **session-end `git show HEAD:<path>` vs disk hash over your own paths** is the only
  thing that catches *others* clobbering *you*.

Neither substitutes for the other. In the same session `ajcr-p2`'s commit reverted my
file for one commit (restored byte-identical) — the hash caught it; the post-commit
stat could not, because HEAD had not moved when I ran it.

**Why:** `commit` writes the whole index as a tree, not just the paths you added, so
the hazard lives in an index you do not control and cannot clean without reverting
other lanes' unstaged work (never `read-tree HEAD` into the *shared* index).

**How to apply:** run both, and at session end enumerate the shared index's staged
deletions with the command rather than quoting any lane's count — the number moves
within a session. A staged `D` on a file you just committed is expected, not evidence
your own procedure broke.

Related: [[postcommit-stat-and-head-hash-are-both-needed]],
[[verified-index-still-races-the-commit]], [[read-tree-commit-race]],
[[hash-your-paths-after-committing]], [[copied-index-is-still-contaminated]].
